title: Audi Q6 e-tron teknik özellikleri ve menzil detayları
summary: Audi'nin yeni elektrikli SUV modeli Q6 e-tron, tek ve çift motorlu seçenekleri, 800 voltluk mimarisi ve 300 milin üzerindeki menzil kapasitesiyle satışa sunuluyor.
body:
Car and Driver'ın aktardığına göre Audi Q6 e-tron, markanın ürün gamında Q4 e-tron ile Q8 e-tron modelleri arasında konumlanan tamamen elektrikli yeni bir lüks SUV seçeneği olarak öne çıkıyor. Beş kişilik oturma kapasitesi sunan araç, hem geleneksel SUV gövde tipiyle hem de daha sportif hatlara sahip Sportback seçeneğiyle tercih edilebiliyor. Model ailesi, arkadan itişli tek motorlu versiyon ve dört tekerlekten çekişli çift motorlu **Audi Q6 e-tron Quattro** seçeneğiyle geliyor.

## Performans ve şarj özellikleri

Tek motorlu standart versiyon 322 beygir güç üretirken, çift motorlu Quattro modeli 456 beygir güce ulaşıyor ve yapılan testlerde 0'dan 60 mil hıza 4,4 saniyede çıkabiliyor. Araç, 800 voltluk bir mimari üzerine kuruluyor ve 94,4 kWh kapasiteli bataryası bulunuyor. Car and Driver'ın paylaştığı bilgilere göre bu batarya, DC hızlı şarj bağlantısı üzerinden yüzde 10'dan yüzde 80 doluluk oranına 30 dakikanın altında bir sürede ulaşabiliyor. EPA tahminlerine göre tek motorlu versiyon 321 mil, çift motorlu versiyon ise 307 mil menzil sunuyor.

## İç mekan ve teknoloji

Q6 e-tron modelinin kokpiti, ön konsolu kaplayan geniş ekran duvarıyla dikkat çekiyor. Standart olarak sunulan donanımlar arasında kavisli 11,9 inç gösterge ekranı ve 14,5 inç bilgi-eğlence dokunmatik ekranı yer alırken, ön yolcu için ise 10,9 inçlik ek bir dokunmatik ekran opsiyonel olarak sunuluyor. Araçta ayrıca sürüş güvenliğini destekleyen otomatik acil frenleme, yaya algılama ve şeritten ayrılma uyarısı gibi standart sürücü destek sistemleri bulunuyor.

**Neden önemli?** Audi'nin yeni elektrikli SUV modeli, benzinli lüks araçları aratmayan konforlu sürüşü ve gelişmiş şarj altyapısıyla markanın elektrikli araç pazarındaki iddiasını güçlendiriyor.

2025 Audi Q6 e-tron / Q6 e-tron Sportback
- Quiet and composed ride, Quattro model offers swift acceleration, lots of available technology features.
- Could be more exciting to drive, overwhelming array of screens, styling blends in a little too well.
- The Q6 e-tron is an refined EV that looks and feels much like a gas-powered luxury SUV, offering good performance and range if not much excitement.

Overview
Shoppers searching for a luxurious electric SUV have quite a few options these days, and Audi has added yet another to the list: the 2025 Q6 e-tron. Slotting between the Q4 e-tron and Q8 e-tron, it aims to be a solution for those who find the former a bit too small and the latter a bit too big. The lineup starts with a rear-drive, single-motor version with 322 horsepower and a claimed 321 miles of range. A more powerful all-wheel-drive, dual-motor version has 456 horsepower and a 307-mile range estimate. The interior is high-tech and handsomely styled, with a curved display screen on the dashboard and sustainable materials used in the upholstery. For something a little more stylish, the forthcoming Q6 e-tron Sportback will offer a fastback body style; a performance-oriented SQ6 e-tron is also offered, but we review that model separately. The Q6 e-tron competes with other EV SUVs such as the Cadillac Lyriq, the Genesis Electrified GV70, and the Lexus RZ.
What's New for 2025?
The Q6 e-tron is new to the Audi lineup, and it will offer both traditional SUV and swoopier Sportback body styles.

EV Motor, Power, and Performance
The Q6 e-tron's standard setup uses a single electric motor that drives the rear wheels and produces 322 horsepower. The dual-motor Q6 e-tron Quattro has all-wheel drive and 456 horsepower. We found that it offers a calm and controlled ride during our initial test drive of the Q6 e-tron with the optional air-spring suspension. It drives similarly to the gas-powered Audi SUVs you're likely familiar with, but it's quieter and more responsive when you step on it. The dual-motor powertrain offers particularly punchy acceleration, but we haven't yet driven the single-motor model. The performance-minded SQ6 e-tron ups the ante with 510 horsepower and a sportier suspension tune, so enthusiast drivers will want to look at that model instead. One of our favorite features of the Q6 e-tron is its predictive regenerative braking system, which uses data collected from a radar system, exterior cameras, GPS, and a road-sign detection system to dial in just the right amount of regenerative braking just when you need it. The system works nearly flawlessly and avoids any unnecessary jerkiness while maximizing energy recapture.
0–60-MPH Times
In our testing, the dual-motor Q6 e-tron Quattro hit 60 mph in 4.4 seconds. We haven't tested the single-motor model yet, but Audi predicts a 60 mph time of 6.3 seconds.
Range, Charging, and Battery Life
The Q6 e-tron uses an 800-volt architecture and features a 94.4-kWh battery, which Audi says can charge from 10- to 80-percent in under 30 minutes on a DC fast-charging connection. The EPA estimates that the single-motor version will go 321 miles on a charge, while the dual-motor Q6 e-tron Quattro is rated at 307 miles. In our range testing, which we conduct on the highway at 75 mph, the Q6 e-tron Quattro managed an impressive 250 miles of range.
Fuel Economy and Real-World MPGe
The EPA rates the standard Q6 e-tron at 104 MPGe combined and the Q6 e-tron Quattro at 99 MPGe combined. We haven't had a chance to take it on our 75-mph highway fuel economy test route. When we do, we'll update this story with real-world test results. For more information about the Q6 e-tron's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.
Interior, Comfort, and Cargo
Like other Audi SUVs, the Q6 e-tron sports a contemporary cabin that is loaded with display screens and convenience features. While the look is undoubtedly modern, we suspect some users may be overwhelmed by the amount of digital real estate. Those folks are still sure to appreciate the attractive materials used throughout the interior, some of which are made from sustainable materials. Although the Q6 e-tron is close in size to the gas-powered Q5 SUV, its wheelbase is over three inches longer, which results in a more spacious passenger compartment. Cargo space behind the second row isn't as generous here as in some other EV SUVs, but the Audi does offer a small "frunk" storage compartment under the hood.
Infotainment and Connectivity
A wall of screens dominates the Q6 e-tron's dashboard. The curved 11.9-inch gauge display and 14.5-inch infotainment touchscreen are both standard, but a third display—a 10.9-inch touchscreen—is an optional extra for the passenger. That screen allows for access to the infotainment system and can also stream video content, the view of which is blocked to the driver while the vehicle is in motion. The software used is a new Android-based interface which, despite its lack of physical buttons, we found easy to adapt to during our test drive of a prototype model. A head-up display and a navigation system with an augmented reality feature are available, as is an 830-watt Bang & Olufsen stereo system.
Safety and Driver-Assistance Features
Audi offers a lot of driver-assistance features as standard, including basics such as automated emergency braking and a driver-drowsiness monitor. More advanced features, including an adaptive cruise control system with a lane-centering feature, are available as options. For more information about the Q6 e-tron's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites. Key safety features include:
- Standard automated emergency braking with pedestrian detection
- Standard lane-departure warning
- Available adaptive cruise control with a lane-centering feature
Warranty and Maintenance Coverage
The Audi Q6 e-tron and Q6 e-tron Sportback will offer the same limited warranty and powertrain warranty as the Q8 e-tron SUV.
- Limited warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Powertrain warranty covers four years or 50,000 miles
- Electric components are covered for eight years or 100,000 miles
- No complimentary scheduled maintenance
